question.text: The students <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>10</mn></msub></math> are to be divided into <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> groups <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>B</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> such that each group has at least one student and the group <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> has at most <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> students. Then the total number of possibilities of forming such groups is __________.

solution.text:
If group C has one student then number of groups

C11029-2=5100

If group C has two students then number of groups

C21028-2=11430

If group C has three students then number of groups

=C310×27-2=15120

So total groups=31650
